entries.title: Dirichlet lattice displacement bridge setup
entries.statement: For a finite nonempty D subset Z^3, L_D has diagonal 6 and off-diagonal -1 for nearest neighbors within D; outside coordinates are fixed to zero. A displacement is u in R^{3|D|}. At reciprocal G in 2pi Z^3, B_{D,G}=|D|^{-1} sum_{x in D} exp(i G dot (x+u_x)). The 3D infinite lattice Green integral is C_3=(2pi)^(-3) integral_{[-pi,pi]^3} [2 sum_j(1-cos q_j)]^(-1) dq.

entries.title: Rejected route: radial convexity implies vector convexity
entries.statement: REJECTED proposed implication: for s>0, scalar convexity of r -> r^(-s) would imply that each vector pair potential |x|^(-s) has a positive semidefinite displacement Hessian. The transverse-Hessian counterexample refutes this implication. This is a record of a false proof route, not an asserted theorem.

entries.title: DRAFT: Riesz pair negative transverse curvature
entries.statement: Author-derived counterexample, pending independent w539 review: for s>0 and x!=0 in R^3, Hessian |x|^(-s)=s|x|^(-s-2)[(s+2)ee^T-I], e=x/|x|. Its two transverse eigenvalues are -s|x|^(-s-2). The path x(t)=(1,t,0) has second derivative -s at zero. This defeats termwise vector convexity, but does not establish instability of a collective lattice or background Hessian.

entries.title: DRAFT: uniform covariance to reciprocal Fourier order
entries.statement: Conditional proof sketch pending w539: assume H_D is C^2 on all R^{3|D|}, even, and Hessian H_D(u)>=kappa L_D tensor I_3 for every u, with kappa>0 independent of D. Under exp(-beta H_D)/Z, beta>0, Re E B_{D,G}>=1-|G|^2 C_3/(2 beta kappa). If this lower bound a is positive, E|B_{D,G}|^2>=a^2 uniformly in D. C_3<=sqrt(3)pi/8. Proof is in w538/ATTEMPT.md. This is a surrogate conditional claim; no actual Riesz Gibbs Hessian, defect-control, labeling, or DLR-limit premise has been established.

entries.title: DRAFT: covariance alone does not fix reciprocal phase
entries.statement: Author-derived counterexample pending w539: on N even nonadjacent sites D of Z^3, L_D=6I. Put H_D(u)=3 kappa sum_x |u_x-m_x|^2, with m_x=0 on half the sites and e_1/2 on half. At G=2pi e_1, its product Gaussian Gibbs law has covariance I/(6 beta kappa) at each site, but E B_{D,G}=0 and E|B_{D,G}|^2=[1-exp(-|G|^2/(6 beta kappa))]/N ->0. Thus a covariance bound without coherent mean phase cannot imply this fixed-mode order bound. This does not exclude all Bragg modes and is not a Riesz Gibbs counterexample.

entries.title: DRAFT: finite Riesz near-collision curvature blocks global convexity
entries.statement: Author-derived obstruction pending w539: for finite N>=2 and s>0, a Riesz pair energy plus a C^2 external/background term near an interior point has a transverse second derivative -s epsilon^(-s-2)+O(1) when one pair approaches distance epsilon and other particles stay a positive distance away. It is negative for small epsilon, so no positive pointwise global Hessian lower bound holds on the full finite-particle configuration space. This does not analyze a renormalized infinite-volume Hessian or the Hessian restricted near a fixed crystal. A controlled-region/complement argument or a nonconvex inequality is required instead.
assumptions: Other particles a fixed positive distance away
External/background potential C^2 with bounded Hessian nearby

entries.title: DRAFT: full-law Bragg input for pressure response
entries.statement: Paired w537 C5, independently rederived by w538 but final w539 review pending: fix beta>0 and complex S_N with |S_N|<=N, circularly invariant full zero-field law and M_N=Re S_N. If p_N(h)=log E exp(beta h M_N)/(beta N) converges pointwise near zero and liminf E|S_N/N|^2>=b^2 for 0<b<=1, then p right slope at zero is at least b. This uses the unrestricted full law, not a conditional chart. A fixed positive real tail gives p(h)>=ha for every a<b. Local UI/tightness, vanishing-field Gibbs closure and lattice classification are separate inputs. Proof and exact peer provenance: w538/PAIRED_AUDIT.md.
assumptions: Pointwise pressure limit on an open interval near zero
Not a theorem proving those Riesz inputs

entries.title: DRAFT: a conditional circular Bragg moment need not yield a cusp
entries.statement: A circular full law with S_N=0 of weight 1-exp(-cN) and S_N=aN exp(iTheta) of weight exp(-cN) has conditional ordered-branch normalized second moment a^2 but full pressure p(h)=max(a|h|-c/beta,0) and p right slope zero at the origin. This author-derived finite-law counterexample is pending w539. It retains circular symmetry and refutes conditional-chart substitution only; it does not refute C5 or Riesz crystallization.
assumptions: Uniform angular phase on the ordered branch
Finite probability law, not a claimed Riesz example

relations.rationale: Draft supporting end: "two transverse eigenvalues are -s|x|^(-s-2)"; rejected-route end: "each vector pair potential ... has a positive semidefinite ... Hessian". Exact contradiction; referee pending.
The bridge explicitly uses L_D, B_{D,G}, C_3 and reciprocal G as defined in this setup.

Returned end: "Hessian V(z) >= Gamma uniformly ... Cov(nu) <= Gamma^{-1}". Bridge end assumes Hessian H_D >= kappa L_D tensor I_3; instantiate Gamma=beta kappa L_D tensor I_3. No missing Riesz premise is supplied by citation.
Target end asks for a "crystalline Gibbs phase"; this obstruction blocks one proposed convexity transfer to that target. It neither refutes nor proves P0309.
Earlier-attempt end: "must control defects, anharmonic fluctuations ... uniformly in volume". This bridge states an explicit uniform Hessian premise and preserves the remaining Gibbs gap.
The bridge end requires evenness/zero mean. This counterexample has the same Hessian lower bound but incompatible mean phases, showing why that premise cannot simply be dropped.

O3 end: "no positive pointwise global Hessian lower bound" for full finite Riesz space. B1 end: "Hessian H_D(u)>=kappa L_D tensor I_3 for every u". B1 remains valid for its convex surrogate, but its direct full-Riesz instantiation is blocked.
B1 gives a bound under "exp(-beta H_D)/Z" in a Dirichlet convex model. C5 requires the "unrestricted full law". Identical Fourier notation does not establish identity of probability measures.

O4 end has conditional second moment a^2 but full-law moment a^2 exp(-cN). C5 end explicitly requires positive full-law liminf. This tests the necessity of the full-law premise; it does not refute C5.
